title: Baechu Kimchi
shortDescription: Napa cabbage quarters are salted until flexible, coated leaf by leaf with a gochugaru, radish, scallion, garlic, ginger, fish-sauce, and salted-shrimp paste, then refrigerated as they ferment.
culturalContext: Baechu kimchi is one of many Korean kimchi traditions and is often simply called kimchi in everyday contexts. Recipes vary by household, region, season, dietary practice, and fermentation preference; this draft does not claim one universal formula.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: About 4 hours 15 minutes, before optional fermentation

equipment: Clean 4-liter glass or food-safe plastic container with headspace

ingredients.preparation: do not substitute table salt by volume

ingredients.item: saeujeot fermented salted shrimp with brine

instructions.heading: Split and salt the cabbage
instructions.action: Trim only protruding core, slit each cabbage through the base, and pull into halves. Wet the leaves, then distribute salt between them, concentrating near the thick white stems.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Salt is distributed leaf by leaf and the cores still hold each half together.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash cabbage under cool running water before cutting and use a clean food-safe basin.

instructions.heading: Turn during salting
instructions.action: Rest 2 hours, turning every 30 minutes and ladling accumulated brine over the cabbage.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The thick stems bend without snapping and the leaves look wilted.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the basin away from raw meat and seafood preparation areas.

instructions.heading: Rinse and drain
instructions.action: Rinse the cabbage thoroughly in several changes of cold water, split into quarters along the core, and drain cut-side down in a colander.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No visible salt remains and water no longer pools between leaves.
instructions.safetyNote: Use potable water and a sanitized colander and sink area.

instructions.heading: Cook and cool the porridge
instructions.action: Whisk water and sweet rice flour in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until bubbling and thickened; add sugar for 1 minute, then cool completely.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The porridge coats the spoon and is fully cool before seasonings are added.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not mix hot porridge with raw vegetables or pack it warm.

instructions.heading: Make the seasoning paste
instructions.action: Mix cooled porridge with garlic, ginger, onion, fish sauce, saeujeot, and gochugaru. Fold in radish, carrot, and scallions.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Vegetables are evenly coated in a thick red paste.
instructions.safetyNote: Wear food-safe gloves and avoid touching eyes; verify fish and shellfish allergens before serving.

instructions.heading: Coat and pack
instructions.action: Spread a thin layer of paste over every cabbage leaf. Fold each quarter into a packet and press into a clean container, leaving at least 5 cm / 2 inches of headspace.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cabbage is compactly packed with minimal trapped air and no paste on the rim.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean, nonreactive food-grade container; never pack to the lid because fermentation can create gas and overflow.

instructions.heading: Ferment conservatively and refrigerate
instructions.action: For a fresher result, refrigerate immediately. For a more active ferment, hold in a cool room for no more than 8 to 12 hours in this unreviewed draft, venting as needed, then refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C.
instructions.temperature: Cool room, then refrigerator at or below 40°F / 4°C
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Early fermentation may show small bubbles and a clean sour aroma; cabbage stays submerged or coated.
instructions.safetyNote: Fermentation duration is pending qualified safety review; discard the batch if mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration appears.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan does not use a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Salted cabbage stems bend without snapping
Early fermentation may create small bubbles and a clean sour aroma
foodSafetyNotes: Use clean hands, gloves, tools, containers, and potable water throughout.
Keep fish sauce and saeujeot refrigerated as directed on their labels and declare fish and shellfish allergens.
Leave headspace and vent a sealed vessel carefully because fermentation creates gas.
Refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C after the chosen short room-temperature stage.
Discard kimchi with visible mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration; normal souring alone is not the same as spoilage.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish and crustacean shellfish; verify gochugaru and other packaged ingredients for facility cross-contact.

substitutions: A vegan kimchi requires a separately developed and reviewed seasoning system; do not simply omit both fermented seafood ingredients without retesting salt and umami balance.
Daikon may replace Korean radish, with texture and moisture differences noted for testing.
ingredientSourcing: Choose dense napa cabbage with crisp pale stems and fresh leaves.
Korean markets stock gochugaru, Korean fish sauce, saeujeot, and Korean radish; inspect allergen and storage labels.
makeAhead: Prepare and cool the rice-flour porridge up to 1 day ahead under refrigeration; prepare fresh vegetables and seasoning the day of assembly.
storage: Keep refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C in a clean container with headspace. Flavor continues to sour; a validated shelf-life claim requires food-safety review, so label the batch date and inspect before use.
reheating: Serve cold or at cool room temperature; do not reheat as a standalone banchan.
leftovers: Use increasingly sour, otherwise sound kimchi in thoroughly cooked dishes only after the final review defines an approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Cut a cabbage quarter crosswise just before serving
Serve in small portions with rice and grilled dishes

faq.question: Can I eat baechu kimchi before it ferments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can be served freshly seasoned, then refrigerated as flavor and acidity develop.

faq.question: Why leave headspace in the container?
faq.answer: Fermentation can produce gas and lift liquid or vegetables, so empty space reduces pressure and overflow risk.
